title: George Lombard Jr.'s late go-ahead homer punctuates Yankees' 6-4 comeback win over Rays
description: Cam Schlittler made his final start of a season worthy of the AL Cy Young, while George Lombard Jr. powered the Yankees to a 6-4 come-from-behind win over the rival Tampa Bay Rays.
fullText:
In the final game of their four-game home series against the Tampa Bay Rays (96-63), the Yankees (92-67) came back from 4-0 down to win 6-4.

-- In the second inning, after allowing a walk to Jonny DeLuca and a single to Richie Palacios with two outs away, Yankees starter Cam Schlittler struck out Ryan Vilade to strand Rays baserunners on first and third and preserve a scoreless tie.

-- The following inning, Taylor Walls drew a leadoff walk. Walls came around to score on the very next at-bat, a single by Yandy Diaz, which became an unearned RBI double when right fielder Heliot Ramos' throw to third base intended to tag out Walls skittered away. Then, Rays star third baseman Junior Caminero laced an RBI single to double the damage in the inning.

-- With the Rays having clinched the AL East division title, Yankees manager Aaron Boone made it clear that he would be limiting the number of pitches his starters throw during the team's remaining regular season games to ensure their arms are fresh for the postseason. Accordingly, with the Yanks still trailing 2-0, he pulled Schlittler for right-handed reliever Michael Fulmer, who opened the fourth inning with a clean frame to work with. Caminero knocked Fulmer out of the game with one out away in the fifth, mashing an RBI double off the left field wall, which scored Diaz. Tim Hill relieved Fulmer and worked into - and more importantly, out of - a bases-loaded jam to hold the Rays to their 3-0 lead.

-- With Luis Gil on the mound for the sixth inning, the Yankees couldn't complete a double play when Gil dropped George Lombard Jr.'s on-target throw to first base. A run scored as a result. In the bottom half of the frame, Austin Wells clubbed a solo homer to cut Tampa's lead to 4-1. Gil pushed onward to record a scoreless seventh inning.

-- Lombard singled home Ben Rice in the bottom of the seventh with a one-out double, before the shortstop added another run thanks to a wild pitch with an acrobatic slide-turned-hop-turned tag of home plate, beating out Rays catcher Liam Hicks. With two outs and Yankees baserunners on second and third, Paul Goldschmidt completed the comeback and tied the game, 4-4, with a single to center field. Cody Bellinger grounded out with runners on the corners to end the inning.

-- Rookie reliever Bradley Hanner handled the eighth for the Yankees. After allowing a leadoff double, he battled back to record a scoreless inning.

-- With the score still tied, one runner on base, and two outs in the inning, Lombard cranked a pitch down the left field line, a moonshot that stayed fair and gave New York a 6-4 lead.

-- Hanner closed the door in the ninth inning, earning his first career win as well as his first career save, sealing the series win for the Yankees, 6-4 the final on Thursday night.

-- Following his brief start on Thursday night, Schlittler's final stats for the 2026 regular season were set in stone. Across 33 starts, Schlittler pitched to the tune of a 1.95 ERA and 0.92 WHIP. He tallied 239 strikeouts and just 47 walks in 193.2 IP. Time will tell whether his sensational season is rewarded with the AL Cy Young Award.

The rookie shortstop was the hero on Thursday night. He tallied three RBI on two hits - a double and a two-run homer, his seventh in just 41 career games thus far - and showcased his athleticism on his improvisational slide, which allowed him to score from third on a wild pitch.

An RBI double for George Lombard Jr.! pic.twitter.com/wIBriD3grw

GEORGE LOMBARD JR. CLUTCH 2-RUN HOMER FOR THE LEAD! pic.twitter.com/c2nuoMyhqW

The Yankees kick off the final series of their regular season, a three-game set at home against the Baltimore Orioles on Friday.

Due to the forecast of sustained inclement weather on Saturday, Friday will see the Yanks and O's play a doubleheader.

The first game is set to begin at 4:05 p.m. and the second game will start no earlier than 7:05 p.m.

New York's starting pitcher in that first game is yet to be announced.

Baltimore will send out Trevor Rogers (4.07 ERA, 1.18 WHIP in 165.2 IP).

title: He is the ATP player who became world number one despite losing six first round matches in a row
description: There have been 29 different men who have held the number one singles ranking on the ATP Tour. Jannik Sinner is the 29th of those...
fullText:
There have been 29 different men who have held the number one singles ranking on the ATP Tour.

Jannik Sinner is the 29th of those world number ones, with his current ongoing reign lasting 24 weeks, having topped the ATP rankings for a total of 90 weeks across his three spells.

Despite this, Sinner is under threat of losing his number one to Alexander Zverev, who has won two Grand Slams this year and is currently on track to end the year as the top-ranked player in men's tennis.

Zverev is now in a similar position to what Yevgeny Kafelnikov was in back in 1999, but he will be hoping that if he does become world number one, it happens in a more successful fashion than it did for the Russian 27 years ago.

Kafelnikov came into the 1999 season as the world number 11, but had previously been ranked as high as world number three.

The Russian very quickly returned to the top 10, as Kafelnikov won the Australian Open, his second Grand Slam title after Roland Garros in 1996.

This propelled Kafelnikov back up to his previous career-high of world number three, as he closed in on the world number one ranking, which was then held by Pete Sampras, who did not play the Australian Open due to physical and mental fatigue.

Kafelnikov continued this form into the indoor season, where he won the title at the Rotterdam Open after beating a young Roger Federer, as well as British players Greg Rusedski and then Tim Henman in the final.

This placed Kafelnikov as the world number two heading into the sunshine double of Indian Wells and the Miami Open, but neither tournament went to plan for him.

Kafelnikov lost his only match at both Indian Wells and the Miami Open, and after winning two matches in the Davis Cup, he was hoping to rediscover his form upon his return to the ATP Tour for the clay court season.

This did not happen for Kafelnikov, who lost in the first round of all four of his next clay-court tournaments. Three of these four players Kafelnikov would lose to were ranked outside the top 60, including then world number 196 Ivan Ljubicic beating him in Monte Carlo.

Despite Kafelnikov losing in the first round of six tournaments in a row, he became world number one after being beaten by world number 72 Richard Fromberg and overtook Sampras, who dropped 144 points after being absent due to a back injury, at the top of the ATP rankings.

Gustavo Kuerten beat Kafelnikov, 0-6 7-6(4) 6-3

Vincent Spadea beat Kafelnikov, 6(6)-7 7-6(4) 6-2

Andrei Pavel beat Kafelnikov, 6-3 2-6 6-3

Franco Squillari beat Kafelnikov, 6-2 6-4

Ivan Ljubicic beat Kafelnikov, 6-1 6-2

Richard Fromberg beat Kafelnikov, 6-4 2-6 6-4

Kafelnikov ended his run of six successive first-round losses at his next tournament in Rome, but his relatively poor form still continued after becoming world number one.

In his four tournaments as world number one, Kafelnikov won just six of his 10 matches, which culminated after losing in the first round of the Queen's Club Championships.

Sampras won the title at Queen's, and therefore dethroned world number one Kafelnikov, who dropped down to world number three after also falling below Pat Rafter.

Tournaments Kafelnikov played as world number one

Third Round – Lost to Gustavo Kuerten (No.14)

Hypo Group Tennis International (St.Poelten)

Semi-final – Lost to Mariano Zabaleta (No.26)

Second Round – Lost to Dominik Hrbaty (No.30)

First Round – Lost to Sargis Sargsian (No.74)

Kafelnikov's one and only run as world number one lasted a total of six weeks, which is one of the lowest in ATP history, equal to Marcelo Rios and Thomas Muster.

Only Carlos Moya (2) and Rafter (1) have had short reigns as world number one, with both also taking place during the 1999 season.

title: QB Marcus Washington Jr. commits to Kentucky Football
description: Kentucky secure a commitment from sophomore quarterback Marcus Washington following the team's upset of Texas A&M.
fullText:
The momentum from Kentucky Football's huge upset win over No. 9 Texas A&M continues for the Wildcats and head coach Will Stein, as the Wildcats have landed a commitment from 2029 3-star quarterback Marcus Washington Jr.

Washington does not currently have a national ranking, as he is only a sopho

The 6-foot, 165-pound quarterback plays for Cajon High School in San Bernardino, California, and chose Kentucky over programs including Arizona, Arizona State, Michigan, North Carolina, Texas A&M, and others.

Kentucky first offered Washington in May and brought him to Lexington for an unofficial visit on Sept. 12. It appears the Wildcats made a strong first impression, with Kentucky's 31-21 upset of Texas A&M helping further solidify Washington's interest in the program.

The Wildcats also have a promising quarterback pipeline for the coming years. Kenny Minchey is expected to lead the team this season and next, while Matt Ponatoski could take over in 2028. 4-star 2027 quarterback Jake Nawrot is also committed to Kentucky, giving the Wildcats another highly regarded quarterback in the pipeline.

Of course, Kentucky could still add another quarterback to its 2028 recruiting class, but the future of the position is already looking bright under Stein.

Washington's recruitment is not necessarily over, and plenty can change during the recruiting process. However, his commitment gives Stein and the Kentucky staff another young quarterback to develop as they continue building the program for the future.

title: Durfee football wins with heavy heart: 'Everything we do moving forward is for Marvins.'
description: Durfee football players honored late teammate Marvins Antoine with an emotional victory. "Everything we do moving forward is for Marvins."
fullText:
FALL RIVER — Matt Sherry and the Durfee High football team played with a heavy heart on Thursday, Sept. 24 against Somerset Berkley.

The Hilltoppers wore the emblem 'MA4' on their helmets in memory of former teammate Marvins Antoine, who was killed in a stabbing last weekend.

For 48 minutes, the Durfee team and Sherry played hard for Antoine.

"Mentally the whole team was in a rough place, especially coming after that news in the morning" Sherry said after the Hilltoppers defeated the Raiders 28-7. "I feel like it defintely brought us together this week. Everything we do moving forward is for Marvins."

Watch MA high school football on NFHS

Sherry threw two touchdowns and ran for another to account for most of the Hilltoppers offense. Sophomore running back Ahliy Cantave rushed for his third straight 100-yard game. He finished with a game-high 134 yards on 18 carries and scored a 47-yard touchdown.

"It has been a tough week for the program," Durfee head coach Taylor Brown said. "We went through real life situations this week. I'm happy for the kids with they way they responded all week. We were only able to practice two days this week. We knew it wasn't going to be easy because Somerset plays until the end. I told the kids to play for Marvins because he was always super competitive when he was out there."

The Raiders (0-3) responded after the Hilltoppers drove the field for a touchdown — a Sherry keeper from 2 yards out — on their first possession. Senior Gavin Gooch took it in from 16 yards out to tie the game at 7-7 with a 1:50 remaining in the first quarter.

The only problem, SBR went scoreless for the last three quarters.

"You can shoot yourself in the foot," Raiders first-year head coach Chris Santos said. "We were playing behind the sticks, penalties and stuff like that. It makes life difficult. I thought my boys played hard. Those guys (Durfee) was playing with a little extra fire today."

Catave's long touchdown run late in the second quarter enabled the Hilltoppers (2-1) to take a 14-7 lead. Sherry then completed a long 45-yard pass to Landyn Nogueira for a touchdown with 39 seconds before halftime to give Durfee the lead at 21-7.

Sherry finished off his brilliant night with 21-yard touchdown strike to James Gondre with 3:59 left in the third quarter.

There was a moment of silence prior to the game to pay homage to Antoine, who lost his life last weekend in Providence, Rhode Island. He was 18 years of age. Since the COVID season, the Raiders hold a 3-2 advantage over the Hilltoppers entering Thursday's contest. Both of Durfee's win came at Somerset Berkley Regional High School.

title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 32 - Pete Chilcutt (1994-96)
description: During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Chilcutt wore only jersey No. 32 and put up 3.9 points, and 3.3 rebounds per game.
fullText:
The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history.

To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day.

With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover.

And for today's article, we will continue with the seventh of 14 who wore the No. 32, Pete Chilcutt. After ending his college career at UNC, Chilcutt was picked up with the 27th overall selection of the 1991 NBA Draft by the Sacramento Kings.

The Sumter, South Carolina native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career with the Kings. He also played for the Detroit Pistons before he signed with the Houston Rockets in 1994. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the (then) Vancouver (now, Memphis) Grizzlies in 1996

During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Chilcutt wore only jersey No. 32 and put up 3.9 points, and 3.3 rebounds per game.

title: JJ Redick addresses Lakers starting lineup then drops viral quote
description: Who will join Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the Lakers starting lineup this season?
fullText:
The 2026-27 NBA season is quickly approaching, and Los Angeles Lakers coach JJ Redick still has questions to answer before training camps begin Monday, Sept. 29.

Redick and Rob Pelinka, the team's President of Basketball Operations, spoke reporters to address where things stand from a roster reconstruction standpoint within the organization.

Redick was clear that guards Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves along with center Walker Kessler are all penciled in as starters for the upcoming season, but position battles remain.

As for the rest of the starting lineup? Redick joked, "The other spots will not be two white guys."

More: Did Lakers lose or win free agency? Grading massive roster overhaul.

Pelinka stated that the team has three clear objectives for the roster this offseason.

The first was re-signing Reaves, who agreed to a four-year, $180 million max contract in July. The team also had aspirations of acquiring a "franchise center" to play alongside Dončić.

Kessler signed a four-year, $130 million deal with the Lakers, but in order to secure the big man, the Lakers needed to send multiple draft assets to the Utah Jazz as part of the trade, including unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and first-round swaps in 2028 and 2030.

Los Angeles went with a youth movement after LeBron James, the NBA's oldest active player and arguably still the league's biggest star, departed and signed as a free agent with the Philadelphia 76ers.

Kessler is 25 years old, and wing Ziaire Williams is 24. Guard Quentin Grimes is 26, while guard Collin Sexton and forward Sandro Mamukelashvili are both 27.

Quentin Grimes is expected to serve as the small forward in the lineup while Jake LaRavia and Sandro Mamukelashvili will compete for the role as the starting power forward.

title: Seahawks safety Julian Love an NFL leader in key stat
description: Seahawks star Julian Love is in a four-way tie for the league lead in interceptions and has the chance to claim the lead for himself in Week 3.
fullText:
Seattle Seahawks safety Julian Love enters Week 3 with an opportunity to break an early-season tie in the NFL's statistical leaderboard and claim sole possession of the league's interception lead.

Love shares the league lead of two interceptions alongside New York Giants safety Jevon Holland, Las Vegas Raiders rookie Hezekiah Masses and Carolina Panthers linebacker Devin Lloyd, per Sleeper Sports.

With four players sitting atop the leaderboard, the race is tight. Another big game from Love in Week 3 may leave him alone at the top of the league, provided his fellow co-leaders do not add as many INTs to their totals.

Love opened the season with an interception in Week 1, helping the Seahawks defeat the New England Patriots 13-10. He then recorded another pick in Week 2. His impact has extended beyond interceptions, as he has contributed in multiple other areas, but his picks stand out.

Love's ability to patrol the field and create disruption figures to keep him as a key producer in Seattle's defense as the season moves forward and gives him a good chance to seize the league lead in interceptions for himself in Week 3.

However, Love's availability for Week 3 is suddenly in jeopardy. He appeared on the injury list for Thursday's practice due to a calf injury and was a non-participant. Seahawks Wire will continue to monitor the situation.

title: It should have happened years ago. Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are finally ready
description: Talk about the fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua has shifted from if the heavyweight bout will happen to what it might look like Dec. 11.
fullText:
Tyson Fury will try to keep Anthony Joshua on his back foot with the jab, predicts Grey Johnson of BoxRec, the official database for pro boxing. Maybe sneak in an uppercut and hurt Joshua.

Joshua, by contrast, will try to box carefully for a bit to get his confidence going, said BoxRec's Johnson. Maybe get in some counters and then he can push Fury around.

In abrupt and welcome fashion, talk around the heavyweight boxing match between Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) and Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) finally shifted from if it will happen to what might happen during a fight between two former world champions.

It's on, and it's a win for boxing.

No gimmicks. No influencers. Just two British heavyweights capable of slugging it out.

Let's get the details out of the way:

Where: Principality Stadium in Cardiff Wales of the United Kingdom.

Time: 2 a.m. local time. 9 p.m. ET.

Streaming: Netflix (free with a monthly subscription.)

Joshua stands 6-6 and for his last fight weighed in at 251 pounds.

Fury stands 6-9 and for his last fight weighed 261 pounds.

In December, Joshua broke Jake Paul's jaw in two places during a sixth-round knockout victory. In July, Joshua knocked out Kristian Prenga in the second round.

In July, Fury's opponent, Mariusz Wach did not bother coming out for the eighth round.

Both Fury and Joshnua are equipped to stop the other with one punch.

Ideally, they would have fought seven years ago. In recent years, both fighters have showed their age.

Joshua, 36, got knocked down twice in the first by Prenga in July before he staved off near-disaster with his second-round KO. He also suffered a brutal knockout loss to Daniel Dubois in 2024.

Fury, 37, got knocked down in 2023 by Francis Ngannou, the former UFC champion who was making his pro boxing debut.

Both Joshua and Fury also have lost two fights to Oleksandr Usyk, the former undisputed heavyweight champion.

Fury and Joshua remain two of the biggest and most charismatic stars in boxing. They have the size and the skill to deliver an electric fight, in front of an expected sellout crowd of 73,000 in Principality Stadium and a global audience on Netflix.

Tyson is the early favorite, and the line could shift before something becomes clear about this fight.

title: Concerning news for Knicks as $276 Million Finals Star Hits Contract Stalemate
description: The New York Knicks are preparing to defend their first NBA championship in 53 years, but a key player faces an uncertain future. Karl-Anthony Towns helped New York beat the San Antonio Spurs in the Finals, but his contract situation remains unsettled before training camp. Towns is eligible for a four-year extension worth up to [...]
fullText:
The New York Knicks are preparing to defend their first NBA championship in 53 years, but a key player faces an uncertain future. Karl-Anthony Towns helped New York beat the San Antonio Spurs in the Finals, but his contract situation remains unsettled before training camp.

Towns is eligible for a four-year extension worth up to $276 million. ESPN's Shams Charania reported that talks have stalled and that an agreement is unlikely before training camp begins.

The Knicks and Towns discussed an extension for much of the offseason, but little progress has been made recently. Talks could continue during the season, although ESPN reported that a deal is not expected soon.

The timing adds pressure to the situation. Towns is entering the final guaranteed year of his contract and will earn $57 million this season. He also has a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 season.

New York has also set a clear financial limit. Owner James Dolan has repeatedly said the Knicks want to avoid the NBA's second apron, which restricts how expensive teams can build and change their rosters. That approach has already come at a cost, as backup center Mitchell Robinson left for the Boston Celtics during the offseason.

Towns enters the contract talks after a strong postseason. He averaged 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists while shooting 55 percent during the playoffs. That production helped New York finish 16-3 and win the championship.

His playoff performance gives him a strong case for a major extension. However, the Knicks also face other costly contract decisions. Josh Hart is eligible for an extension, while Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby could become eligible next offseason.

New York must now balance two goals. The Knicks want to keep their championship team together, but they also want to avoid pushing the payroll beyond the limit they have set.

Towns remains under contract with the Knicks for the coming season. The main question is whether New York can find a number that keeps its championship core together without crossing its financial line.

fullText:
The California Supreme Court excoriated Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco over his seizure of hundreds of thousands of Proposition 50 ballots earlier this year, ordering the former gubernatorial candidate to immediately hand over all remaining materials in a pair of scathing decisions Thursday.

"We hold that the seizure of the ballots was unlawful," wrote Chief Justice Patricia Guerrero. "While allegations of election improprieties are a very serious matter, our Elections Code contains numerous established mechanisms for investigating and proving misconduct that do not compromise the integrity of voted ballots — contrary to the means employed here."

California voters overwhelmingly passed Proposition 50 in a special election last fall, blessing a new congressional map that all but eliminated Republican districts in response to gerrymandering efforts in Texas and other deep-red strongholds.

Bianco, a popular MAGA personality and former Republican candidate for governor, doggedly pursued claims the Riverside County returns were fraudulent, seizing on a discrepancy between the registrar's voluntary hand tally and the official vote count to commandeer the ballots as evidence of a crime — a move the court roundly rejected.

"A criminal prosecution commences only upon the occurrence of certain events — none of which has occurred in this case — and may only be initiated by a public prosecutor," Guerrero wrote. "But even if a criminal prosecution had commenced, allowing for a court-ordered production, [the law's] plain text prohibits the removal of the ballots from the registrar's physical custody."

The ruling comes less than two weeks before Californians will start casting ballots in the race for governor and a handful of bitter congressional contests — nationally-watched elections that would be vulnerable to similar interference unless the court gave clear orders, advocates warned at oral arguments last month.

"It's bound to be repeated again," said Chad W. Dunn of the UCLA Voting Rights Project, which led the first of two related suits against Bianco.

California Atty. Gen. Rob Bonta, who brought the other suit, cheered Thursday's rulings as an important electoral safeguard.

"The Court has now made clear that this kind of defiance cannot stand," Bonta said in a statement following the twin decisions. "I encourage Californians to make their voices heard and vote early in the fast-approaching November 3 midterm elections, with the confidence of knowing that their voted ballots will never again be subject to physical seizure by rogue county sheriffs."

Bianco did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Bianco has long flirted with President Trump's election fraud conspiracy movement. Though the ballot seizures in February were widely seen as a campaign stunt, the legal theory behind them — that local lawmen can commandeer voter materials from elections officials, and that sheriffs are unanswerable to officials who outrank them, including attorneys general — belongs to a larger "constitutional sheriffs" ideology.

California's seven Supreme Court justices appeared by turns perplexed by and incredulous of those theories during oral arguments last month.

"You are walking into a very dense thicket of very specific laws that govern elections in particular and I think it's a very established cannon of interpretation that the specific trumps the general," said Associate Justice Goodwin H. Liu.

Thursday's rulings effectively short-circuited Bianco's efforts to keep the ballot probe alive.

"Bianco presumably could have used traditional investigatory tools, within the bounds of the law, to obtain other evidence of election-related crime," Guerrero wrote.

Further, the court said, Bonta's authority to stop both the seizure and the ad hoc recount was unequivocal.

"Respondents' arguments all boil down to the unsustainable view that the state's chief law enforcement officer ... must remain a mere bystander to an unprecedented sheriff's investigation of undeniable statewide significance," Guerrero wrote. "As we have explained, that is not the case."

In a footnote, justices also took a swipe at Bianco's initial effort to have the case tossed for lack of standing — a move apparently undertaken on the legal advice of an elaborate AI hallucination, reminding lawyers of their "professional duties of competence and candor."

The ballot battle emerged from a Riverside County pilot program meant to boost voter confidence — a handwritten tally that ultimately fell about 46,000 votes short of the official count, sparking claims of fraud.

The registrar of voters met with the county board of supervisors and the citizens' group behind the claim and carefully explained how the discrepancy emerged. Yet, Bianco pursued warrants to seize more than 650,000 ballots, alleging they were evidence in an investigation of wide-ranging misconduct.

When he learned of the warrants, Bonta ordered Bianco to stand down. Instead, the sheriff accelerated his plans, dispatching armed deputies from Riverside County's Special Investigations Bureau, Emergency Response Team and SWAT unit to sweep up the votes.

Later, Bianco directed his underlings to begin counting those ballots by hand — a potential felony under state law, which forbids anyone other than election officials from so much as touching a ballot container.

When Bonta again ordered him to stop, Bianco argued the attorney general had no authority to command him, later claiming in court that the law conferred only an "advise and consent" role.

Spurred by the Riverside dustup, lawmakers in Sacramento recently passed a "raft of additional legislation" to shore up ballots and empower elected officials to protect them in the future.

"It is a lot to ask of our election officials that they not only do their jobs competently but also stand ready to sue anyone who unlawfully interferes with their duties. Yet here we are," Liu wrote. "For our democracy to flourish, our elections must be conducted in accordance with the law."

fullText:
Nolan Wells died after going on a boat trip with friends on the 4th of July.

The family of Nolan Wells on Thursday released the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy report, which found that the cause and manner of death are "undetermined."

"This 18 year old male was found face down in the water at Horn Island. Because the circumstances surrounding this death are unknown, the cause and manner of death are best classified as undetermined," the state autopsy report states.

The state autopsy report indicated that the pathologist found "evidence of injury" to the back on Wells' head that is described as "two dark red-purple subcutaneous scalp contusions."

The report did not conclude how this injury occurred. It also found that there were "no external scalp injuries" and "no fractures" in the skull.

The State Medical Examiner's office report comes after a grand jury reviewing the evidence in Wells' death found that no criminal charges are warranted at this point, according to the report released on Monday night.

The state autopsy report's conclusion matches the findings of the private autopsy commissioned by Wells' family, which was released in July. It preliminarily ruled his cause and manner of death as "undetermined pending investigation," with the independent pathologist acknowledging multiple limitations in the report.

"Losing a child, it truly breaks your heart ... especially someone like Nolan, who brought so much joy and light and life to everyone," Wells' mother, Christine Wonsley, told reporters in July.

"The only question we have is, what happened to our son?" she said.

The circumstances surrounding Wells' death garnered national interest after the college football player went missing on the 4th of July after going on a boat trip with friends to Horn Island. Officials said it appeared Wells stayed behind on the island after his friends left.

The teen's body was recovered on July 6, and authorities said they suspect he drowned.

Jackson County Sheriff John Ledbetter said there was no initial indication of a crime, but he stressed that investigators were "working diligently to determine exactly what occurred."

Ledbetter also said the sheriff's office welcomed the family's independent investigation.

ABC News' Sabina Ghebremedhin contributed to this report.

fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 24 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday, with talks on trade and artificial intelligence and the growing strategic rivalry between the countries all in the spotlight during an elaborate state visit.

Here are some major takeaways from ‌the talks:

The US secured an extension of its trade truce this week - but only a short one.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two sides agreed ‌to extend by two months a trade agreement that ended last year's trade war and was due to expire in November. The extension would give Washington and Beijing "more time to see what we can do on the economic front," he said.

But ​rather than locking in a durable agreement, the extension appears to push the central questions — tariffs, Chinese purchases, rare-earth supplies and technology restrictions — into the next round of negotiations.

Bessent said on Wednesday that Beijing was meeting its requirement in the earlier agreement to buy 25 million tons of soybeans but was lagging on its pledge to buy $17 billion in other agricultural goods. US officials have said rare-earth deliveries were also falling short, another sign that significant gaps remain.

For companies, the result is a familiar form of instability: tariff rates remain lower for now, but decisions must still be made against a shifting policy backdrop.

For ‌Trump, Xi's White House visit was an opportunity to show off ⁠a Washington being remade in his image.

After Xi treated Trump in Beijing to a tour around a Ming dynasty temple and a walled-off garden retreat rarely opened to foreigners, the US president returned the favor with a different kind of spectacle: Troops wearing wigs and tri-corner hats marched in formation and played music in ⁠a Rose Garden redesigned to look like a Trump golf club.

Fighter jets and bombers roared overhead during ceremonies staged on Wednesday and Thursday, one so loud it caused Trump to flinch.

When the White House press corps was called to cover the two leaders, it wasn't to hear them talk about the weighty affairs of state. Instead, it was to watch them tour the Marine One helicopter and the recently redesigned South Lawn of the ​White ​House, replete with a large helipad emblazoned with the presidential seal.

Speaking to reporters, Trump brushed away questions about ​their policy discussions.

"He loves good granite," Trump said of Xi. "Great meeting."

XI WANTS US 'PRUDENCE' ‌OVER TAIWAN

As expected, Xi pressed Trump on the Taiwan issue, saying, according to China's official news agency, that China hoped the United States would "handle the Taiwan question with prudence."

The agency's English-language service also wrote that Xi hoped the US would oppose Taiwan independence.

That would be a tougher version of Washington's long-standing formulation that it does not "support" independence. There are no signs that the Trump administration plans to change its wording.

There was no immediate White House readout of the exchange, but US officials have long avoided explicitly stating opposition to Taiwanese independence. Any shift in language would raise questions about Washington's resolve to defend the island and provoke opposition in Congress.

Xi, not for the first time while meeting Trump, invoked the "Thucydides Trap", an academic theory that competition between a rising power and an established one tends ‌toward war.

While the Chinese leader said the risk "can be overcome," his reference underscored how concerns about a potential US-China ​military conflict continue to shadow relations between the world's two largest powers.

Xi argued that both nations stand to gain from ​cooperation and lose from confrontation, and he called for regular military dialogue and stronger crisis-prevention ​mechanisms.

Trump, for his part, drew on the two nations' shared history to emphasize the potential for cooperation. They could accomplish much by pursuing common interests, he ‌said, invoking their wartime alliance against Japan.

The two leaders expressed diverging ​views about artificial intelligence.

Trump, who has declared that AI ​should be called super intelligence, or SI, said in a social media post that he wants to "to leave it exactly where it is" and rely on the US Department of Justice rather than impose any new guardrails. He insisted that China held the same position.

But Xi said on Thursday that, as leading nations on AI, China and the US must ​manage its growth.

"We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and ‌manage AI for good, and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people," Xi said.

Some of the biggest ​names in AI were expected to attend Trump's state dinner at the White House on Thursday for Xi, including Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Nvidia's (NVDA.O) Jensen Huang.

(Reporting ​by Simon Lewis, David Brunnstrom and Trevor Hunnicutt; Editing by Ross Colvin, Alistair Bell and Sanjeev Miglani)

title: I Tested the Apple Watch's New Heart Rate Sensor to See If It's Really Better Than Garmin's
description: I pitted the Apple Watch Series 12 against the Garmin Forerunner 570.
fullText:
Apple caught my attention with their claim that the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 have the “most accurate heart rate in a wearable.” It’s hard to make a really accurate heart rate sensor, and in my experience, Apple hasn’t had a great track record in that area. So I tested the Series 12 pretty intensively over the past week or so, and now I have results.

I’m picky about accuracy; longtime readers have seen me test watch after watch against my trusty chest strap to find out how good each one really is. That sometimes brings surprises: The Powerbeats Pro 2 are surprisingly bad at heart rate tracking if you have small ears, for example. I also discovered that the Garmin Forerunner 570 is shockingly good at heart rate accuracy, far better than any other device I had tested up to that point. (Garmin’s Forerunner 970 and the newest Fenix and Venu watches have the same sensor.)

Is the new Apple Watch really good enough to beat Garmin’s best sensor? Apple believes it is, but I doubted that claim, for a few reasons. The first is simply Apple’s track record. Early models of the Apple watch had better sensors than most wearables at the time, so Apple developed a reputation for good accuracy. For example, back in 2019 or so, the Series 4 watch performed far better for me than the Whoop 3.0. But time marches on, and devices have gotten better. Garmin has an excellent sensor, as I already explained; the Pixel watch is also impressively good. But Apple just didn’t keep up.

You can see it in my comparisons over the years: here’s the Series 11 glitching where a Garmin did just fine, and here’s the Series 10 struggling alongside a Fitbit Charge 6. If I were to rank all the heart rate sensors I’ve tested for their accuracy, the Garmin 570 would be A-tier, the Pixel Watch and most good sports watches would get a B, and the Apple Watch (Series 10 and 11) would be a C. (S-tier would be reserved for chest straps.) Not long ago, I got downvoted to negative infinity for commenting on Reddit that Apple’s heart rate accuracy (up to the Series 11) is “mid at best.” Sorry, but it’s true.

But, OK, perhaps it’s a new era. Apple redesigned its optical heart rate sensor to include larger LEDs and arrange them more closely in a circle. To support its claim that the new sensor is the most accurate on the market, it published a study that was extensive in its breadth (seven recent, competing devices were tested in a variety of activities) but limited in usefulness. Each pairing of a device and workout type was given, essentially, one number. We don’t get to see how each device behaves in use. The data feels cherry-picked, and in any case, it doesn’t give us enough information to say whether one sensor is truly better than another, or specifically what it does better. So I’m going to add my own data points.

I am just one person, so my experiments amount to a very small, informal study. That’s the case for any tech reviewer, no matter their qualifications—so feel free to compare my data to what others have found, but keep these limitations in mind for each of us.

I took the Apple Watch Series 12 and the Garmin Forerunner 570 out for several tests during workouts. (I did not have a feasible way of testing background measurements outside of workouts.) I wore one device on each wrist, positioned according to manufacturer recommendations, and, at the same time, used an electrical chest strap to provide the reference values.

I have relatively light skin, which may improve accuracy, and no wrist tattoos, so both sensors should get a clear signal on either wrist. I have six-inch wrists, on the small side of average, so I wore the 42-millimeter size of each watch (both are available in larger sizes for those who prefer it). A good fit is critical to getting good accuracy, and I feel I achieved that for both devices. I did my best to have both devices equally snug (but not uncomfortably tight) against my wrist.

I tested both devices, together, on treadmill runs, outdoor trail runs, a rowing session, and a few strength sessions. Some of these workouts involved quick changes in intensity, leading to peaks and troughs in the graph. Others were more steady. Gripping objects such as dumbbells or rower handles can interfere with accuracy for some devices, which is why I included those workouts. Ambient light and temperature can affect accuracy as well, so I tested in a variety of weather conditions.

In my first set of tests, which I also shared here, the Apple Watch and the Garmin both performed well, but each had their flaws. The Garmin sometimes lagged a bit at the start of the interval, but quickly caught up. The Apple Watch didn’t have that problem, but sometimes missed the highest values on small spikes in heart rate. I’d call this one a tie.

In my other trail runs and treadmill runs, I saw a similar pattern: Both watches would be on track most of the time, but each had their quirks. Garmin was more likely to miss out on the beginning of spikes, but the Apple Watch was more likely to drop data points entirely, especially toward the beginning of a workout.

One day, I did three mini workouts at the gym: a treadmill run, a rowing session, and a strength session. The strength work included a few sets each of overhead barbell press, front squats (with my arms in a clean grip), and dumbbell curls. Here are those graphs, again with the Apple Watch in red, the chest strap in gray, and the Garmin this time in purple:

Both devices performed equally on the treadmill run, with their own minor glitches but both getting the job done pretty well. On the rower, the Garmin struggled more, missing almost half of the second interval. The Apple Watch wasn’t perfect, though, overestimating in a few places and not always picking up the lowest value between intervals.

The strength workout was a mess for both devices. The Garmin often read low, but the Apple Watch sometimes read high and reported fewer values in total. This view shows it a bit better (each data point is a dot):

Looking at my data, I think the biggest news is that Apple is no longer lagging when it comes to heart rate accuracy. The Series 12 is a lot more accurate in my tests than the Series 10 or 11 ever were. Apple has built a very good heart rate sensor, and they deserve huge credit for that. I will no longer have to tell people Apple's sensor is mid.

But does it have the best heart rate sensor? I’m not so sure I’m convinced. It is holding its own against Garmin’s best sensor, for sure, and that’s impressive. In the rare cases the Garmin struggles, the Apple is usually there with a more-or-less correct value. But I have seen near-perfect graphs from the Garmin on its best days (admittedly, outside of this testing week); I've never seen one quite like that from Apple. The Apple Watch's sensor sometimes has trouble ramping up to correct values at the beginning of a workout; it overestimates on occasion; it doesn’t get all the way down to low values when intervals change quickly; and I’m concerned about the sparseness of the data points. It almost seems like the Apple Watch won’t report a value it’s not sure of, which is arguably better than recording a data point that could be wrong, but leaves odd gaps in some of the charts.

This leads me to over-analyze the claim of  “most accurate in a wearable.” If Apple’s sensor fails to report a data point where another device reports an incorrect one, does that make Apple “more accurate” because more of its data points were on the right line? That’s probably a fair claim, but it still doesn’t feel great to award that device the “best” title. And if we truly want to compare the Apple Watch to all wearables, shouldn’t we consider chest straps, which are also worn, and which are objectively more accurate than any optical sensor in a watch?

After all this analysis, I have a hard time awarding the Apple Watch a definitive title of being the “best” at wrist heart rate accuracy. But it’s damn good, and I have to put it up in the A tier with the Garmin. Congratulations, Apple. You managed to tie the best watch sensor out there, and I can’t claim there’s another one that’s better.

title: 'Don't put pressure on us' over Israel games - Republic of Ireland's Ogbene
description: Republic of Ireland winger Chiedozie Ogbene urges the public to not "put the pressure on us" over the campaign to boycott the upcoming Nations League games against Israel.
fullText:
Republic of Ireland winger Chiedozie Ogbene has urged the public to not "put the pressure on us" over the campaign to boycott the upcoming Nations League games against Israel.

The sides are due to meet in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday before the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October (both 19:45 BST).

Since the sides were drawn together in Group B3, there has been increasing calls in Ireland to withdraw from the games due to the ongoing situation in Gaza with a 'Stop The Game' campaign gathering pace.

In the lead up to Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in Pristina stand-in captain Dara O'Shea confirmed the players would meet on Friday to discuss their approach to Sunday's 'home' game for Israel, which will have no Irish fans in attendance before their behind-closed-doors match the following week.

"I'm aware of the feelings towards it," Ogbene told RTE Sport after Thursday's loss.

"It's a complicated and very difficult task. I just want to say and I hope people don't put the pressure on us to be answering difficult situations.

"There are people who can make the decisions and you can't rely on footballers to make those decisions. That's my feeling on it but as a group we will look at it and will see what we're going to do."

Republic of Ireland deservedly beaten by Kosovo

Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations (UN).

While the upcoming Israel games dominated discourse in the build-up to the Kosovo defeat, Ogbene does not accept that was a reason for a disappointing display in Pristina.

"I know there is a lot of discussion about things like that, but we just tried to focus on Kosovo today," said Ogbene.

"All our mindset was on Kosovo to win this game and then deal with that's coming."

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side had just two chances throughout the game with goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher making some fine saves, while Kosovo efforts were cleared off the line before the hosts finally broke the deadlock seven minutes from time through Vedat Muriqi.

It is yet another slow start to a Nations League campaign for the Irish and Ogbene accepts "it wasn't good enough", while also disappointed he was off-target with a big opportunity in the opening half.

"I thought we may have had enough quality to see it out at 0-0, but overall, it was poor from myself and poor from the standards we set ourselves," he reflected.

"I need to do more. I tried to focus on the ball and just mishit it, but I need to do better.

"We're overly disappointed with the result but most of all the performance as it's not like us."

title: NBA's first MVP Pettit dies aged 93
description: Bob Pettit, one of the earliest stars of the NBA and the first man to win the MVP award, has died aged 93.
fullText:
Bob Pettit, the first man to receive the NBA's MVP (most valuable player) award, has died aged 93.

Pettit won the award twice, in its first year in 1955-56 and again in 1958-59, when he topped the scoring charts in both seasons.

The Basketball Hall of Fame confirmed Pettit's death, describing him as "a true giant of the game".

He was also named an NBA All-Star in all 11 of his seasons and was the first player to reach 20,000 points.

Having starred for Louisiana State University (LSU), Pettit was signed by Milwaukee Hawks in the draft in 1954.

The team then moved to St Louis, and Pettit stayed with them for the rest of his career which included winning the NBA title in 1958 with victory over the Boston Celtics.

He reached two more finals with the Hawks in 1960 and 1961, and retired in 1965 with a career average of 26.4 points and 16.2 rebounds per game.

Pettit was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1971 and had his number 50 jersey retired at LSU in 1954. He was the first of their athletes to ever receive the honor.

LSU paid tribute to Pettit on their website, saying: "Pettit defined what the modern power forward should be in the NBA and set standards that have been hard to duplicate in professional basketball."

title: How PSG's Ballon d'Or duo are pushing each other on
description: While there can only be one winner, team-mates Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are backing each other to win the Ballon d'Or.
fullText:
Paris St-Germain won almost all before them last season, so it's no surprise the team's best are up for the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

The French and European champions have 10 players shortlisted for the greatest individual prize in football, which will be awarded at a ceremony in London on 26 October.

While there can only be one winner, team-mates Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are backing each other to collect the prize.

Speaking exclusively to BBC Sport, they have even suggested sharing the award.

"We can cut it in two," joked Dembele, before adding "honestly, he [Kvaratskhelia] deserves it, the season he had was exceptional".

Kvaratskhelia told BBC Sport journalist Julien Laurens: "Of course it's him [Dembele], the season he had last year, he deserves it."

The pair's reaction won't surprise PSG fans, who watched the duo ruthlessly and selflessly link up on countless occasions during their side's Champions League title defence last season.

So, how do they complement each other's game so well, and could the race for this year's Ballon d'Or be a PSG one-two?

This could be year I win Ballon d'Or, says Mbappe

When will Africa get its next Ballon d'Or winner?

How is the Ballon d'Or winner decided?

PSG made just one signing in January 2025, the last window before their first Champions League title later that year, and it was to bring in Kvaratskhelia for £59m from Napoli.

The then 23-year-old Georgia forward was already a hero in Naples, nicknamed 'Kvaradona' by supporters during Napoli's 2022-23 title-winning campaign.

Full of flare, technically superb and forward-thinking, Kvaratskhelia's play was once compared to George Best by Italian legend Gianfranco Zola - although Kvaratskhelia himself cites Cristiano Ronaldo as his biggest inspiration.

Like his idol, Kvaratskhelia has an impressive work-rate and winning mentality. PSG have won 10 trophies out of a possible 12 since his transfer.

"[He's] electric," team-mate Dembele told BBC Sport.

"Every time he has the ball something can happen. Every time he goes one v one, he provokes the opponent.

"He has shown all his quality. Especially last season where he had a really, really good season.

"Thankfully we didn't let him go to the Premier League."

Kvaratskhelia was named the Champions League's best player of last season, his 10 goals and six assists meaning he averaged a goal contribution in Europe's premier club competition every 72 minutes.

And he did most of his best work towards the business end of the tournament, becoming the first player to score or assist in seven consecutive knockout appearances in a single Champions League campaign.

Kvaratskhelia says his motivation comes from his father, who played for Dinamo Tbilisi and the Azerbaijani national team.

Like his father, Khvicha started his career at Tbilisi before playing for Lokomotiv Moscow and Rubin Kazan in Russia, until Russia's invasion of Ukraine prompted a move back home - to Dinamo Batumi, and then on to Napoli.

"I think for the big nations it's really difficult to understand what [winning a Ballon d'Or] would mean for the small country [like Georgia]," Kvaratskhelia told BBC Sport.

"It's something that is very far, it's like impossible, of course I will be the happiest guy because I want to make my family and country proud."

While defenders double up to deal with Kvaratskhelia on the left wing, France forward Dembele is finding even more joy down the right.

The 29-year-old's blistering pace and cool finishing helped him to a combined 31 goals and assists last season which, thanks to a low workload in terms of gametime, worked out to 1.27 goal contributions per 90 minutes.

Only Harry Kane boasted a better rate among players in Europe's top five leagues last term.

The current Ballon d'Or holder, Dembele also scored six goals in 10 appearances for France in 2026 as his side reached the semi-finals of the World Cup.

"He's an amazing player," Kvaratskhelia told BBC Sport.

"The way he leads the team is important, the way his personality and what he gives the team on the pitch is really incredible, and the season he had last year, it was amazing.

"I think we understand each other very, very much. It's easy to understand what he will make and you just have to make some move and he will give you a ball wherever he wants and wherever you are waiting."

Dembele's goal threat by now is well-known and at PSG he has shown the quality that persuaded Barcelona to once pay a £135.5m to sign him from Borussia Dortmund in 2017.

It may not have worked out in Spain but it meant PSG were able to pick up Dembele for a bargain £43.5m in 2023 and, since Kylian Mbappe left for Real Madrid, the Parisians have made Dembele their main star.

"I didn't change," Dembele added. "I played my game, last season and the one before when I won the Ballon d'Or, I stayed the same person.

"When you win it for the first time, you don't want people to say that you were lucky. So you want to continue to be at the top."

If not PSG duo Dembele and Kvaratskhelia, then who?

Well, England captain Harry Kane is actually odds-on to win after a club record 61 goals in 51 games for German double winners Bayern Munich last season. He also scored six times at the World Cup.

Lamine Yamal, who won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, is second favourite - followed by his club and international team-mate Rodri.

Real Madrid forward Mbappe scored 42 goals in 44 games for his club last season and won the World Cup Golden Boot with 10 goals on his way to becoming the World Cup's all-time record goalscorer.

Meanwhile, Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi, who is looking to win his ninth Ballon d'Or, has also been nominated.

As has Dembele and Kvaratskhelia's team-mate Ferran Torres, who scored Spain's winner in the World Cup final.

The Ballon d'Or is celebrating its 70th anniversary, with the choice of venue - in London - a tribute to the first winner, Englishman Sir Stanley Matthews.

title: Uefa fears impact of Premier League spending on transfer market
description: Uefa believes "a clear two-speed system" is emerging in the transfer market due to huge spending by Premier League clubs this summer.
fullText:
Uefa believes "a clear two-speed system" is emerging in the transfer market as a result of the huge spending by Premier League clubs this summer.

In its latest European club talent and competition landscape report, European football's governing body laid bare just how dominant the transfer activity of English clubs has become.

Uefa's report said that the estimated €4.6bn (£4bn) spend by Premier League clubs is "larger than that of the next eight largest European countries combined".

Andrea Traverso, Uefa's executive director of finance, said that this trend "raises concerns".

"Transfer values continue to rise sharply, particularly in the English market, increasing future pressure on club financial results," Traverso wrote.

"These developments also point to an increasing concentration of talent and a growing polarisation of the market, with the emergence of a clear two-speed system.

"English clubs were involved in more than 60% of the deals and paid an average of around €24m (£20.7m) per inbound player, compared with only around €4m (£3.4m) to €5m (£4.3m) in the other major European leagues, underlining a widening gap in purchasing power."

Traverso said that any "correction in transfer values" or "slowdown in buyer demand" could have serious implications for any club carrying debt.

The report added that the transfer spend of the 20 Premier League clubs this year is "equivalent to 56% of their annual revenue" - much higher than the 33% average of the pre-Covid decade.

Uefa also highlighted the increasing trend for English clubs to do big-value transfers between each other, which showed a 44% increase to €1.55bn (£1.33bn).

The English domestic market was "as large in fee value as the next five market flows combined".

A market flow describes league-to-league deals. After the English domestic market, the next most lucrative was the German Bundesliga to the Premier League, at €690m (£594m).

The number of European transfer fees paid above €50m has significantly increased, from 14 in the summer of 2024 to 23 in 2025. In 2026 there was another jump to 35 such deals, of which Premier League clubs were responsible for 29.

With pressure to pass financial regulations, clubs have increasingly looked to sell academy players as they provide pure profit on the books.

European clubs generated an estimated profit of €6.8bn (£5.85bn) on these sales over the summer, an increase of €655m (£564bn) on 2025.

Uefa also found little evidence of clubs using multi-club ownership structures to move players for inflated or reduced fees.

Total transfer fees of such deals were €152m (£130.8m) with an estimated market value of €159m (£136.8m).

More than half of this spend came from transfers between Chelsea and Strasbourg.

title: Barcelona's Deco denies interest in Man Utd's Gabriel
description: Barcelona sporting director Deco says the club is not interested in Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel.
fullText:
Barcelona's sporting director Deco said the club has no interest in pursuing Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel, 15, travelled to the Spanish city after informing United that he wanted to leave Old Trafford earlier this month.

Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris St-Germain are among the clubs reportedly keen on securing his signature.

"There's nothing to say about this boy," Deco said at a news conference.

"It's normal we always have players linked with us. There's a huge market for that, even when they are young.

"We are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that.

"First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

Gabriel has not trained at United since scoring a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut on 10 September.

Tournament rules prevent him from playing for a side other than United in this season's competition.

But if he obtains a European Union passport through either his father - a former Republic of Ireland international - or mother, who has Greek-Cypriot heritage, he could join a club in the EU when he turns 16 on 6 October.

Last week, United manager Michael Carrick urged for people to be "careful and sensible" about the amount of exposure and scrutiny given to the youngster.

title: Man Utd borrow another £90m as debt tops £1.1bn
description: Manchester United confirm they have borrowed another £90m since 30 June, to take their overall debt to more than £1.1bn.
fullText:
Manchester United have borrowed another £90m since 30 June - and confirmed they spent £191.7m on new players this summer.

United bought Andrey Santos from Chelsea on 13 July, Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa on 14 July and Carlos Baleba from Brighton on 25 August.

The fees the club stated they spent on the trio at the time the transfers were announced added up to £153m, and it is not clear where the additional sum has been spent.

The club have been approached for comment.

Confirmation of the additional borrowing of £90m was included in a more detailed filing to the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, following Wednesday's release of their 2025-26 accounts to 30 June, and showed their overall debt was still more than £1bn despite major cost-cutting measures implemented by Sir Jim Ratcliffe since he became minority owner in 2024.

United confirmed it made three further drawdowns from its revolving credit limit, on 29 and 31 July and 28 August, totalling £120m. It then paid back £30m on 21 September.

It takes United's overall debt to £1.15bn, made up of the historic debt, which now stands at £578m, the £200m outstanding on its revolving credit facility, and £375m in outstanding transfer fees.

That is a £72m reduction on the £447m they stated was owed in transfer fees in the 2024-25 accounts. However, it remains a large sum, with £104.8m due in between one and two years and £51.9m in between two and five years - with the remainder due in the next 12 months.

The club say payments for their most recent transfers "are due within the next five years".

title: US edge opening session of Presidents Cup
description: The US begin their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team on day one.
fullText:
The United States began their bid to win an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup by opening up a 3-2 lead over the International team at the end of Thursday's fourballs matches at Medinah Country Club in Illinois.

Justin Thomas and rookie Jackson Koivun put the first point on the board for Brandt Snedeker's American team with a resounding 4&3 win over Canada's Corey Conners and Colombia's Nico Echavarria.

World number one Scottie Scheffler, who was partnered with his long-time friend Sam Burns, took the 17th hole and held on to close out their victory over Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, who were left to rue several missed putts down the stretch.

And two-time major champions Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa ensured the US would take an advantage into Friday's five foursome matches.

Clark and Morikawa led from the opening hole against Australia's Adam Scott and reigning Open champion Ryan Fox before completing their 3&2 success with two holes to spare.

"A session win is a session win; we're going to take it any way we can get it," said Snedeker.

However, Geoff Ogilvy's International side will head into the alternate shot format on Friday with optimism of remaining in contention to claim only their second ever triumph in the biennial contest, some 28 years after their first in 1998.

Japanese duo Hideki Matsuyama and debutant Ryo Hisatsune recorded a 3&1 success over Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele, while Kim Si-woo and Tom Kim always looked comfortable in their 3&2 win over Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay.

The five foursome matches scheduled to take place on Friday will be followed by two sessions on Saturday, split between four four-ball matches in the morning and four foursomes in the afternoon.

All 12 players on each team will then compete in the singles matches on Sunday, with 15½ points required for overall victory.

title: Bellamy wants more from Wales after loss to Portugal
description: Craig Bellamy believes there is "more to come" from his Wales side in the Nations League following their opening-match loss in Lisbon.
fullText:
Wales earned plaudits but Craig Bellamy wants more from his side, after admitting they were forced to suffer in their narrow 1-0 defeat in Portugal.

Joao Felix's deflected strike proved enough to earn victory in Lisbon for the hosts, who also saw Cristiano Ronaldo's effort ruled out by VAR.

It was a winning start to the Nations League title defence for Portugal and for new manager Jorge Jesus.

Despite being under pressure for long spells in Lisbon, Bellamy's injury-hit side ended strongly as Brennan Johnson and Lewis Koumas both went close to snatching a draw.

"It was a difficult game for us. We had to suffer a lot," said Bellamy.

"I think that's the longest we've been in a game without the ball.

"We could have done more with the ball but I'm beyond proud as well.

"We have a lot of players who weren't here. That's OK, we can handle it.

"A lot of players who don't play, week-in, week-out. So for them to use the energy they were able to, we've got to have a big heart to be able to do that. They've always shown that and they showed that again."

Felix strike earns Portugal narrow win over Wales

When Bellamy watched on as Ronaldo caused lockdown

Wales have a short turnaround to their second League A fixture against Denmark in Copenhagen on Sunday (17:00 BST).

But Bellamy feels his squad - missing Harry Wilson, Karl Darlow, Dylan Lawlor, Joe Rodon and Nathan Broadhead through injury - are capable of improving.

"There's more for us, so that's something we always look at as a positive," he said.

"How can we improve? How can we get better?"

Ronaldo unsurprisingly took the spotlight in the build-up to the contest at Jose Alvalade Stadium - where the 41-year-old began his professional career with Sporting in 2002.

The forward missed a big opportunity and had a goal disallowed for offside, which would have been his 980th top-flight goal, before being substituted midway through the second half.

He could well line-up against Wales again when Portugal play the return match in Cardiff in November.

Amid the noise around the Al-Nassr frontman, Bellamy refused to be overawed and hopes to face Ronaldo again.

"If you looked at everything that was going on, it's a £1.4bn squad you're up against, [but] I felt quite calm. The players give me that," added the Wales boss.

"Ronaldo is one of the greatest players of all generations, not just this generation.

"You have to plan for him because he's beyond dangerous, even at his age.

"He's a superstar and I'd love to think I'd have the opportunity to be up against him again, but I don't know, maybe time is ticking."
